key_insight: DermDepth shows that single-view photos can be turned into metric-scale 3D skin reconstructions, enabling more precise lesion and wound measurement without extra hardware.
clinical_relevance: This could improve dermatology workflows by adding 3D size and surface detail to routine imaging for monitoring skin cancers, wounds, and morphology changes.
method: Trained a monocular 3D model on D-Synth, a new synthetic dermoscopy dataset with pixel-perfect 3D labels.
Combined dermoscopic and macroscopic training to predict depth, metric scale, and surface normals from one image.
Fine-tuned on a small set of real clinical samples to improve generalization across diverse real-world skin cases.
evidence_signal: According to the abstract, training on D-Synth reduced metric scale error on real dermoscopic data from over 16x to under 1.1x and was evaluated on three real-world benchmarks spanning millimeters to hundreds of centimeters.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful fine-tuning and validation across camera types, skin tones, and clinical settings before real-world deployment.
paper_title: DermDepth: Toward Monocular Metric Scale 3D Reconstruction Models for Dermatology
